operations.comment: ; iNES header: mapper 1, 128 KiB PRG and 128 KiB CHR; no trainer. Kept verbatim to preserve cartridge identity.
; Initialize CPU, wait for PPU warmup, clear RAM through $07EF, install the intro script and enable rendering. Lower PRG pair is fixed; calls may select upper banks.
; All active work runs through NMI; foreground spins here.

; Restore SP from SavedCpuStackPointer, push saved return PC high/low and status, restore A/X/Y, then RTI. Caller must supply writable save cells and a valid return stack/PC; no writer or observed entry is established.
; Enter update while the busy flag sign is clear; reject a nested/reentered update while it is set.
; Return directly from the interrupt.

; Divide updates by the signed countdown, advance the frame tick and disable rendering before dispatching the first NMI continuation. Later entry restores scroll/mask, polls input and runs the second continuation.
; A:Y selects a replacement script descriptor; enter its first handler.
; Advance the four-byte script descriptor and dispatch its little-endian handler pointer. The shared epilogue clears NMI busy state.

; Load pointer pairs and palette from the selected upper-bank resource header, expand its PPU stream, then select scene graphics. The later entry advances the stage or installs the ending script at stage index five.

; Create the stage rescue/destination assignments, clear completion and phone state, then advance the four-byte script. The following handler removes the chosen destination from the masks and saved slots; when more targets remain it selects the next stage script. The final entry jumps to the descriptor address in argument bytes 2/3.
; Replace ScriptDescriptor with the little-endian descriptor argument and immediately dispatch the replacement; do not advance the old record.
; Read a delay from descriptor byte two, then install the countdown continuation.
; Decrement once each four frame ticks; continue the script when the delay reaches zero.
; Choose the audio-wait NMI continuation; the nonzero high byte makes this branch unconditional.
; Disable APU channels and wait using the input gate continuation.
; Keep the script waiting while any music channel remains active; the zero case joins script advancement.
; Track Start in the input latch; leave the script waiting while it is released.
; Advance once on a newly pressed Start; a held key remains latched.

; Disable/update the shared NMI work, copy the descriptor argument into the second continuation and return through the interrupt epilogue. The second entry prepares scene state before common screen setup.

; Choose scene/audio setup by handler entry. Stage-indexed resource pointers and a selected music request feed the common screen setup; mapper calls change upper PRG context. Clear the course/text overlay before initializing the selected view.
; Select the stage index before loading its resource pointers.
; Install palette/OAM transfer as the first NMI continuation, clear scroll and nametable select bits, enable background, then start the next script descriptor.

; Install a split NMI pair: refresh the screen first, then latch a new Start press. A held button does not advance repeatedly; release clears the latch. While waiting, service upper-bank input work only when audio state is idle.
; Update scene decorative objects under the established scene-bank mapping.
; Choose one of two scene records by stage parity.
; Select the other scene record before joining descriptor initialization.

; Take a record pointer from the descriptor or parity selector. Save its command stream after the six-byte header. Header tags $FD/$FE/$FF select saved position, alternate continuation or retained scene state.
; Restore position and scene coordinates from persistent RAM; use the fixed vertical placement.
; Load five header fields. $FE changes the second NMI continuation; $FF preserves the scene selector.
; Switch the second NMI continuation to the alternate scene entry.
; Replace the scene index unless the header explicitly preserves it.
; Service scene audio before normal frame work.
; Select the normal resource bank, detect a fresh Start press and route to the phone/menu script when allowed.
; Latch Start and either open the menu or clear the scene flag and install the alternate descriptor.
; Join the shared script screen-command completion path.
; Release the Start latch, fetch the scene command and dispatch through its doubled index in the upper-bank handler table. Shared continuation advances records and resumes the actor update.
; Consume one command operand as the script wait timer, then advance the command stream.
; Wait on the command timer or trigger a state transition from the scene flags; advance the command only when the gate completes.

; Command handlers consume actor selectors and coordinate operands from (ReadPointer),Y. FE derives a selector from the current scene; FF uses the selected rescue location. Indexed coordinates may be absolute or signed relative values; orientation selects addition/subtraction with carry through the horizontal pair. The final comparison selects a four-byte skip when actor coordinates differ.
; Compare two position fields against command operands; mismatch selects a three-byte response record.
; Keep the current command while both position fields match.
; Compare vertical placement; mismatch selects a two-byte response record.
; Keep waiting on the matching placement.
; Use the command response index and signed orientation flag to choose synthesized controller bits.
; Choose the mirrored response cell.
; Store the selected input bits and enter the regular actor update.
; Six response masks indexed by the command response shifted right once, with orientation mirroring. Ends before the next command handler.
; Clear scene mode, restore descriptor advancement and reset NMI dispatch.
; Commit the pending display updates and join the foreground dispatch.
; Advance the saved command pointer by the length indexed by its opcode, carrying into the high byte.
; Load the scene palette before actor initialization.
; Reset player state, select callbacks and palette, then clear companion actor slots one through five. Arrays use the actor index X; callback pointers are split low/high arrays.
; Six little-endian actor callback words; initialization of slots 1..5 uses the five suffix entries.
; Select the normal resource bank and jump through player callback slot zero.
; Clear bit 1 in the player action and shared mode flags before the adjacent continuation.
; Select the player form from scene-indexed resource tables, install its callbacks and initial animation/speed state. Upper PRG selection is changed by the form loader.
; Gate input by player flags and cooldown. A/B edge latches trigger actions; direction bits select an even direction code. The shared tail accelerates/decelerates movement and advances animation.
; Count down input suppression and continue movement.
; Test the A button before the B path.
; Latch A; require the corresponding action flag and accumulated readiness before queuing action bit two.
; Install the vertical-action callback, reset its acceleration accumulator, clamp initial speed to at least 32 and select the airborne frame before entering its update.
; Release the A edge latch, then test B.
; Latch B and enter the alternate action when its readiness counter permits.
; Release B when absent, saturate both readiness counters at $40 and decode directions according to orientation.
; Swap direction responses when the orientation sign bit is set.
; Use the idle animation at zero speed; otherwise reduce speed before motion.
; Subtract four without underflow; alternate entries select horizontal directions.
; Choose the vertical direction and enter acceleration.
; Initialize the walking animation and its timing when starting from rest.
; Increase speed by two up to the configured limit. Animation delay depends on speed divided by sixteen; wrap at the animation end.
; Return the animation cursor to its configured first frame.
; Pass speed into the shared movement routine.

; Form-driven movement callback graph. Restore saved companion coordinates, load the secondary form descriptor and accelerate or brake signed speed under directional input. Descriptor fields select animation tables, speed bias, terrain limits, airborne state and landing callbacks. Action transitions install the next callback explicitly; scene-dependent form changes preserve player coordinates across companion setup.
; Speed-indexed delay rows followed by two four-cell directional frame maps. Separate bases at 8AED, 8AFD, 8B06, 8B0E and 8B12 have distinct index domains.

; While A is held and readiness remains, consume readiness in steps of four and increase the action accumulator up to 32. On release/exhaustion install the decelerating continuation. Convert signed velocity to fixed point and integrate the split height before the common position update.
; Finish signed height integration. Clamp underflow to zero, then dispatch the form-specific landing callback through the saved pointer; that target depends on the selected form.
; Latch B, install the alternate callback/animation, clear its counter and queue action bit four.

; The first RTS closes the previous callback. The next entry charges the B action in steps limited to 64, then advances timed animation states. Final completion jumps through the saved form callback; its domain remains local to the form table.
; Hold B to convert readiness into charge, saturating at 64; release installs the timed action animation.

; Count down the animation delay, then dispatch the saved selected-form action continuation. The established eight-row table and explicit override target accepted lower-bank code; arbitrary selectors and natural use remain unproved.
; Initialize the form-specific repeat count and frame delay with zero horizontal speed.
; Cycle frames five/six at eight-update intervals for the form-specific repeat count.
; Use frame seven for the longer completion pause before restoring frame five.
; Wait the last delay and resume the selected form callback without adding a return frame.
; Use actor slot zero; decrement the motion cooldown before shared coordinate integration.
; Reduce the remaining motion cooldown.
; Double speed into a 16-bit delta, save coordinates, and dispatch on even direction codes 0/2/4/6. Coordinates are split fractional/whole arrays, with an extra horizontal high byte.
; Start positive horizontal integration; the continuation propagates carry through the three coordinate cells.
; Propagate the horizontal addition through its high byte and build a probe two units ahead before the shared collision test; carry is supplied by the preceding fragment.

; Integrate negative horizontal or either vertical direction with carry/borrow propagation. Build probes two units around the resulting position, then reject blocked movement through collision helpers.
; Test the opposite vertical edge; bank restoration is shared on successful movement.
; Check actor overlap and both horizontal probes at plus/minus two units.
; Complete the second horizontal collision test before restoring the bank.
; Call the saved-position restoration helper when a collision returns zero.
; Restore the saved upper bank, or probe player coordinates with the selected terrain bank and preserve the result across bank restoration.
; Select resource bank two before terrain inspection.
; Initialize the collision mask; player mode and cooldown can bypass terrain collision.
; Apply the additional player-only collision bypass flags.
; Return the shared nonzero permissive result.

; Build a terrain-map pointer from horizontal position and map base, index by tile row, then combine the cell with a vertical mask. Non-player actors reject cells with bit zero set; the shared helper tests the scene coordinate bounds.
; Finish the preceding mask predicate, then test the saved probe against the scene horizontal bounds and sign-dependent vertical limit. A rejected bound joins the shared failure result.
; Return $FF for the permissive/nonzero result.
; Return zero for the blocking result.
; Sixteen terrain masks indexed by probe Y divided by sixteen, followed by five three-cell overlap extent/slot columns.
; Skip overlap checking if no comparison slot is selected.
; Compare signed coordinate deltas against asymmetric per-type extents. Inside the box, dispatch the selected interaction callback; outside it, return nonzero.
; Restore player index zero and return a nonzero result.
; Three little-endian interaction callback words, selected by the collision dispatcher. Bodies use the actor/interaction ABI; the table ends at the first callback.

; Require the relative height to lie in the narrow interaction band, then request audio, set interaction mode and install player/linked-actor callbacks. Return with X=0 and a nonzero predicate when accepted.
; Set up the transition only when player mode bits $60 are clear; return actor index zero.

; Reject an elevated player. Otherwise choose the selected actor resource/text pointer, increment its bounded inventory counter, queue text and install the interaction callback. Mapper selection is restored by the shared helpers.
; Save the form selector and select resource bank five before resolving its descriptor.
; Double the saved form index into the resource pointer table, cache the descriptor and return to the fixed resource bank for the remaining form fields.

; Load per-form speed/charge limits, animation callback, descriptor and two saved action continuations from parallel byte tables. These pointers describe the selected form; arbitrary bytes are not global callback roots.
; A scene flag chooses fixed parameters or stage-indexed defaults.
; Use the two stage-indexed parameter loaders.
; Set both current and target pairs to 2,1.
; Ignore actions while scene-update bit 2 is set. Otherwise Y is a byte offset into the nine-word action table; dispatch through shared scratch without an extra return frame.
; Nine little-endian action callback words. Y is a byte offset supplied by interaction records; the table's finite extent does not prove every possible selector is valid.
; Read the current pair from stage-indexed tables; exact game meaning is unresolved.
; Two entries load either stage-dependent pair into the current scene parameters. Their game meaning remains uncertain; each pair is copied without arithmetic.
; Read the target pair from the same stage-indexed tables.
; Two entries load corresponding stage-dependent pairs into the target scene parameters.
; Initialize current and target parameter pairs together.
; Tail-call the target parameter loader.
; Apply one of the two stage parameter choices to both the current and target pairs.
; Eight six-byte arrays supply the current/target parameter-pair callbacks for six stages. The numeric values are established; their game-level meaning remains uncertain.
; Eight six-stage arrays: four low-byte rows followed by four matching high-byte rows. Each consumer chooses a pair by its established bases.

; For active slots 1..3, install the callback selected by Y while preserving caller X. Separate entries unlink actors matching the saved slot and resume their direction state, or clear matching links in the three auxiliary slots.
; For slots one through three, clear links matching the saved source slot and restore the packed direction callback when enabled.
; Clear matching linked-slot fields in reverse order without modifying callback state.
; Skip scene updates in scene mode or when scene flag bit one is clear.
; Require the scene update enable bit.
; Return when the scene update is disabled.
; Every sixteen ticks approach target parameters by bounded per-stage increments. Handle the expired scene timer, then cycle companion slots and service enabled actor animation timers.
; When the animation timer expires and speed is nonzero, derive a new delay from the speed high nibble, wrap within the four-frame range and move in the current direction.
; Advance through companion slots; the later entry begins proximity-dependent actor placement.
; Carry the collision predicate into the shared recovery path.
; Use the saved horizontal difference sign to choose the appropriate recovery continuation.
; Select the actor resource bank and evaluate the finite contact list before dispatching the actor callback.
; Copy the split callback fields for slot X into scratch and tail-dispatch. X continues to identify the actor throughout the callback ABI.
; Limit placement attempts to two; derive an aligned position near the player from the slot offset table.
; Propagate the horizontal carry into the high coordinate and run the placement predicate.
; A nonzero placement predicate chooses a fresh actor direction.
; Bound retries with the shared counter, adjust the snapped horizontal coordinate and test placement. Exhaustion joins the shared actor reset path; success resumes the caller state.
; Randomize the low variant flag, clear the enable state and choose a direction callback before resuming actor dispatch.
; Four placement values indexed by actor slot in the nearby placement helper.
; Copy actor coordinates into probe scratch with a temporary negative vertical offset, then check scene terrain.
; Accept the terrain predicate first, otherwise test actor contacts before selecting the next vertical probe.
; Raise the trial vertical probe in steps of 16 until its signed limit; zero is the exhausted result.
; Return the preceding predicate; the next entry replaces direction bits while retaining the variant and movement-mode bits.
; Replace the direction/mode bits from A while retaining the independent variant and movement bits.
; Recover the direction selector from packed animation flags, keep the independent mode bits and install its callback from the direction table.
; Compare a random byte with the first stage-dependent threshold to select a direction family.
; The second threshold divides the remaining random domain into the other two direction families.
; Preserve the chosen family in scratch; a nonzero global override supplies the actual callback index.
; Transfer the explicit override to the callback table index.
; Install the selected direction callback, clear its link and pack the family/callback selector with the retained variant bit.
; Eight little-endian motion callback words followed by six stage speed bytes for stages 0..5.
; Initialize stage-dependent speed, timed frames 6..9 and pursuit callback, mark the actor active and probe its available directions.
; Start ordinary pursuit with quadrant selector zero.
; Initialize the alternate pursuit callback and flags, probe directions and start the comparison with the alternate quadrant bit.

; Subtract linked-actor coordinates from this actor into signed horizontal and vertical differences. Convert negative magnitudes and encode their signs in the quadrant selector for direction selection.
; Negate the two-byte vertical difference and set the corresponding quadrant bit.
; Compare absolute horizontal and vertical distances, preserve actor X and choose a direction family according to the dominant axis and pursuit mode.
; Resolve the negative-difference case against the alternate-pursuit bit before entering the available-direction selector.
; Use the quadrant table to try the preferred direction and a perpendicular candidate. A blocked or close candidate enters the shared detour logic.

; Inspect alternate direction probes and distance thresholds. Choose a viable straight direction, install a temporary detour callback when the target is close, or fall back to a randomized pause when no candidate is available. The neighboring six direction lookup rows map the quadrant/mode index to directional probes.
; Restore actor X, encode the direction and continue movement. The second entry performs one corrective move and restores the quadrant index for further comparison.
; Six eight-cell rows selected by direction/quadrant and alternate pursuit mode. Each value 0..3 identifies a directional probe.

; Set stage speed and frames 0..3, install the wandering callback and probe four directions. Preserve a viable heading; otherwise use one random bit to prioritize alternate directions. When every direction is blocked, enter the timed pause.
; Six stage-indexed speed values, increasing from 24 to 33 in steps of three.

; Save the blocked direction in the height-fraction overlay and move along the alternate one until the original probe becomes available. Restore ordinary/alternate pursuit from flags; the failure entry stops movement and waits a stage-dependent randomized interval before wandering resumes.
; Retry the blocked heading after moving perpendicular to it; resume pursuit once the probe opens.
; Stop movement, display frame four and choose a short stage-dependent delay plus a random low nibble.
; Six stage-indexed delays, decreasing from fourteen to four in steps of two.

; Actor callbacks use X as slot. Install delayed animation, turn or spawn continuations; timers select bounded frames and eventually rejoin ordinary pursuit. The linked-slot value scales the turn delay.
; Clear the selected actor enable/state byte.
; Install the ordinary actor update callback and rejoin the shared lifecycle.
; Select the resource bank used by terrain probes; the continuation samples all four movement directions.

; Convert speed to a fixed-point probe distance and test offsets on both axes. Combine terrain and actor-contact predicates into the four direction bytes. Small secondary probes offset the orthogonal axis by two pixels to avoid accepting only a narrow edge.
; Return immediately when the first orthogonal terrain test is clear.
; Move the probe four pixels across the orthogonal edge before the second terrain test; the next entry performs the analogous horizontal adjustment.
; Return immediately when the horizontal orthogonal edge is clear.

; Finish the opposite horizontal terrain probe, then test two table-selected actor candidates. Compare signed horizontal displacement against plus/minus four pixels; candidates outside that band are skipped before the vertical check.
; Two candidates come from the actor-specific contact table. Compare signed position differences against the narrow horizontal and vertical contact bands.
; Accept contact only when the signed vertical displacement lies in the matching four-pixel band.
; Try the remaining finite candidate, then restore actor X and return nonzero for no contact.
; Restore actor X and return zero for contact.
; Four rows of four candidate actor slots used by the contact search; zero cells are retained exactly.

; If the selected packed inventory count is nonzero, alternate output slots 4/5, unlink the reused slot and decrement the count. Initialize the spawned actor's frame, height, direction and coordinates relative to the player, using the charged action accumulator as speed.
; Signed little-endian horizontal offsets followed by vertical offsets selected by the even directions 0,2,4,6.
; Select bank five for auxiliary callbacks.
; Dispatch split callback pointers beginning at slot four.
; Save/integrate actor coordinates, test scene bounds and restore the saved position when rejected.
; Advance through slots four to six; return at seven.

; Integrate signed vertical velocity and subtract the selected acceleration while rising. When the falling height underflows, clamp to ground, stop motion and install the selected landing callback before the shared coordinate update.
; Six acceleration bytes, four little-endian landing callback words, then four animation-frame constants. Some consumers overlap table views; the exact original array organization is uncertain.
; Acceleration values.
; Landing callbacks; two values share the same entry.
; Initial frame constants.

; Install linked pursuit callbacks for eligible actors. Subsequent callback entries play bounded animation sequences, clear completed slots, change companion behavior or install delayed removal; all rejoin the common actor update.
; Start a second bounded frame sequence; completion clears this actor and updates its companions.
; Queue completion sound, set the companion restore flag and clear auxiliary links before delayed callback reset.
; Check proximity to the player before an auxiliary actor update.
; Preserve the slot index across a nearby update helper.
; Restore the saved actor index before the adjacent interaction continuation.
; Clear the actor enable flags and restore its idle callback.
; Continue the auxiliary actor loop.

; Run delayed removal, companion pursuit and timed frame cycles. Special entries accelerate slot 6, wait for its completion predicate, or animate a linked pair; cleanup restores scene/player state. The final entry loads a selected resource palette/descriptor while preserving mapper context via save/restore helpers.
; For eligible slots one through three, install alternate pursuit and point each link at the completed actor.
; Enable the actor and cycle frames 27..32 with eight-update timing.
; Advance the current frame at eight-update intervals; its configured end determines completion behavior.
; Prepare the slot-six acceleration callback.
; Store the prepared low callback byte for slot six, reset player speed and initialize its auxiliary animation.
; Increase slot-six speed to 160, derive its animation delay from speed and continue until the completion predicate clears.
; Begin the drop callback with animation selector FF.
; Store the prepared animation selector, then initialize negative vertical velocity and signed height for the drop callback.
; Integrate the signed height until its sign changes, then clamp to ground and enter delayed completion.
; Begin the paired sequence with action sound bit 6.
; Request the prepared action sound and disable the main actor while the selected slot runs a timed paired sequence.
; Select resource bank five, load the indexed palette and descriptor, then restore the previous bank.
; Subtract actor X from player X with fractional borrow; compare signed distance against the slot-specific extent. Return $FF inside the extent, zero outside.
; Return zero for out-of-range.
; Return $FF for in-range.
; Seven per-slot extent bytes consumed by the actor movement/probe helper.
; Expand speed into a fixed-point delta and dispatch by even direction code: horizontal positive/negative or vertical positive/negative.
; Add the fixed-point delta across the three horizontal coordinate cells.
; Subtract the horizontal delta; the following entry adds the same fixed-point delta to the two vertical cells.
; Subtract the fixed-point vertical delta. The following entry begins a text request by storing its selector.
; Set player transition mode bits before computing scene-aligned coordinates.
; Save the audio selector, double it into Y and advance the random state; the adjacent code completes text selection.
; Bound the inventory result, restore the resource bank, set the message flag and fetch the selected text pointer; completion continues in the following classified fragment.
; Store the text selector and set the player request bit before the shared text setup continuation.
; Round the scene coordinate into the aligned transition origin, set the transition phase, then expose a separate renderer bank-call entry.
; Call the renderer with effective bank five selected by the preceding entry, then restore the previous bank.
; Fill unused OAM-shadow entries with $F8 from byte four onward. A later entry selects audio sequence zero.
; Defer audio selection while the low timer byte is nonzero; otherwise select scene-dependent audio.
; Leave the current audio state unchanged.
; Use a fixed audio index in scene mode, otherwise derive it from the scene selector.
; Convert scene index to the paired audio index.
; Select bank seven for the audio engine. Y=0 chooses its dispatch operation while X retains the caller-selected audio index.
; Invoke the upper-bank audio entry and restore the previous bank.
; Merge request bits into the audio mailbox at $0372 and return.
; Two entries OR action flags into separate mailboxes. A third snapshots indexed actor coordinates into collision scratch.
; Restore the five saved coordinate bytes to actor X. The second entry copies the current coordinates to the probe tuple without changing their fixed-point representation.
; Return twice A in the 16-bit delta scratch pair.
; Sign-extend the input byte, then shift left four places into the shared two-byte fixed-point delta. Flags preserve the resulting high-byte sign.
; Supply an all-ones high byte before the common fixed-point shift.
; Shift the byte/high-byte accumulator four times and return the two-byte delta in WorkLo/WorkHi.
; Increment the selected packed decimal inventory byte unless it already equals its per-type maximum.
; Six packed decimal maxima used by the bounded increment helper; counts must remain in the caller-supported decimal domain.

; Increment the low decimal digit, carrying at ten into the high nibble. The separate decrement entry requires carry set, borrows into the high digit and replaces an underflowed low digit with nine; neither routine checks the whole-byte domain.
; Install A:Y as second continuation and the normal display-update entry as first continuation.
; Choose descriptor advancement by default. The alternate entry installs A:Y as descriptor pointer and the dispatch entry as second continuation.
; Clear background-enable in the PPU mask shadow.
; Set background-enable in the PPU mask shadow.
; Clear sprite-enable in the PPU mask shadow.
; Set sprite-enable in the mask shadow. The separate palette-reset entry fills 32 shadow cells with color $1D.
; Double scene index, select resources and fetch its palette pointer.
; Read a little-endian pointer from the scene palette table; join the second palette-half copy.
; Copy sixteen colors from A:Y to the first palette-shadow half.
; Copy sixteen colors from A:Y to the second palette-shadow half.
; Copy only colors eight through fifteen of the second palette half.
; Copy through the end of the sixteen-color sprite palette half.
; DMA OAM shadow page two, then upload all 32 palette colors at PPU $3F00. A later entry restores CHR selectors and resumes display update.
; Clear zero-page 48..104 inclusive before initializing course/text state; the overlay meanings depend on the active mode.

; Clear 2048 bytes from PPU $2000. Separate entries fill a specified PPU range and expand signed run/literal packets until the source end pointer. Negative headers repeat one byte; nonnegative headers copy header+1 literal bytes. Later entries initialize and resume a buffered incremental decoder with a callback pointer and chunk limit.
; Save the literal-copy continuation when the output chunk fills before the current packet ends.
; Select the first transfer record and recover the pending byte count for the following transfer loop.
; Advance the packet source, stop at its end pointer and install the completed callback. A separate entry uploads buffered rows at a 32-byte PPU stride; a zero chunk count does nothing.
; Subtract the vertical delta and wrap borrow into the 240-line scroll domain.
; Add the vertical delta; wrap at 240 lines.
; Remove one 240-line screen from the scroll shadow.
; The first entry returns. The following entry doubles the horizontal delta, subtracts it and toggles the nametable on borrow.
; Toggle horizontal nametable selection on scroll wrap.
; Return after horizontal scroll subtraction.
; Double the horizontal delta, add it and toggle the nametable on carry.
; Toggle horizontal nametable selection on scroll wrap.
; Return after horizontal scroll addition.
; Subtract A from the zero-page pointer selected by X; correct the 30-row nametable layout when bit ten changes.
; Correct the low byte by 192 after crossing the nametable row boundary; the adjacent continuation adjusts its high byte.
; Finish the wrapped vertical PPU-address addition by adjusting the high byte.
; The first entry returns. The next adds A to an indexed pointer and checks for the nametable attribute area.
; When a row address enters the attribute area, remove 192 from its low byte; the adjacent continuation adjusts its high byte.
; Finish the wrapped vertical PPU-address subtraction by adjusting the high byte.
; Return from indexed PPU address adjustment.

; A is horizontal delta; X indexes a zero-page PPU address pair. Subtract with borrow, compensate a bit-5 row crossing by 32, and toggle nametable bit 10. Scratch $2C/$2D is clobbered; no live caller is asserted.
; Add A to the indexed pointer; crossing a 32-column boundary removes the row carry and toggles horizontal nametable bit ten.
; Convert the tile pointer at zero-page X into an attribute-table pointer at zero-page Y. Derive coarse coordinates and choose $23C0 or $27C0 by nametable bit ten.

; Upload two split tile rows from descriptor pairs, merge attribute bytes through a preservation mask, then upload both attribute runs. A separate readback entry reads the same descriptors into RAM, explicitly discarding buffered PPU reads before each retained byte.

; Write A low bit first to the MMC1 control register in five stores. Entry requires a ready serial latch, bit 7 clear and bits 2..3 equal 10 (mode 2), keeping physical lower banks 0/1 mapped through the fifth write and RTS. Arbitrary A can remap this code on the fifth write and needs a separate continuation contract.
; Save the selector and serially write its five low bits to MMC1 CHR register zero. This selector is a mapper value, not an effective physical bank index.
; Save the selector and serially write its five low bits to MMC1 CHR register one.
; Save the current upper-PRG selector, then select A. This one-level save slot is shared; nested calls must preserve it separately.
; Restore the saved upper-PRG selector through the shared serial writer.
; Select upper-PRG register value one through the shared writer.
; Record the selector and write five bits least-significant first to MMC1. Effective 8-KiB bank context must be resolved from mapper mode separately.

; Advance the 24-bit right-shifting feedback state with polynomial bytes $1D/$87/$2B. The separate controller entry strobes both ports and collects eight button bits, combining the two low serial data bits for each port.
; Twenty-four one-hot/zero bytes form two overlapping sixteen-selector mask arrays starting at A3AD and A3B5, used for low/high rescue inventory bits.

; Install readback and update continuations, prepare split-row transfer descriptors and run a five-step transition. Later entry restores the saved script, sprite position and resource bank; this appears to animate the menu/text overlay.
; Join the shared frame-completion path after restoring the prior scene bank.

; DMA OAM and upload prepared split rows. A separate entry installs overlay continuations, sets tile/attribute buffers and iterates five groups, choosing attribute nibble masks by phase and tile alignment.
; Four alternating F0/0F masks, then four low callback bytes and four high callback bytes. The high-nibble callback begins at A50A and shares the mask suffix.
; Shift the packed inventory byte four times, then fall into the shared low-nibble mask.
; Extract the low attribute nibble and join the output store.
; Move the low nibble to the high half before masking.
; Store the high attribute nibble. Later entries transfer OAM/rows and begin a palette fade by clamping each saved color luminance to the current fade step; completion enters the input/text update.
; Dismiss the overlay, or periodically update a displayed value while the player flag is set; exact displayed quantity remains unresolved.
; Store the selected packed inventory count and request the associated sound before continuing.
; Resume the frame or clear the value-update flag and begin an input cooldown.
; Wait for input release during overlay cooldown, then handle fresh A or B presses using shared button latches.
; Clear the overlay wait flag, latch A and route according to text-state flags.
; Release A and test B before its edge handler.
; Clear wait state, latch B and choose dismissal, alternate script or text paging from the text-state sign/overflow bits.
; Release B and finish this frame.
; Choose another text page or script continuation. The later directional entry marks a saved flag and clears text/overlay wait states.
; Change player mode from overlay wait to transition and conditionally reset scene audio.
; Clear the transient audio mode before updating scene audio.
; Select the usual return descriptor.
; Select the alternate return descriptor.
; Install the chosen descriptor and reset the overlay sprite position before transition.
; Clear the alternate text mode and take the unconditional branch to the text setup path.

; Validate packed page counters, increment or reset the current page, then form a stream pointer from the base plus four times the page and initialize the text reader. Exact page-selection semantics remain tentative.
; Read a low/high continuation pointer from the text stream, preserving byte order across the second read; load the next script address for the following setup.
; Install the descriptor continuation, invoke the renderer and finish the interrupt. Later entry transfers OAM/palette and conditionally writes the updated value to PPU.
; Write one value at the saved PPU address while the display-update flag is set.
; Resume CHR/display update. A separate entry sets tile/attribute buffer pointers and derives the overlay origin from current scroll minus eighty lines.
; Wrap the overlay origin into the 240-line domain.

; Derive the horizontal strip PPU address from scroll, correcting the 240-line vertical domain according to orientation.
; Apply the sixteen-line correction after vertical borrow.

; Resolve each cell to a nine-byte metatile record: eight tile bytes plus one attribute byte. Choose four tile bytes and the appropriate attribute nibble for each of eight cells. Advance scene coordinate by sixteen per cell. A later entry begins vertical-strip address preparation.
; Select the backward edge path.
; Sample 128 units ahead of the scene origin, with orientation-dependent sampler selection.
; Join the reverse sampler; a separate entry adjusts the PPU destination by one tile row.
; Sample at the current scene origin and choose sampler by orientation.
; Join the alternate map sampler.
; Resolve the map and trailing cells, then build fifteen vertical samples with an unrestricted index mask.
; Use an eight-cell wrapped index and resolve the vertical transfer descriptors.
; Resolve the leading cell pointer from the scene map.
; Build eight samples, switch sampler and then extend the strip through sample fifteen.
; Resolve nine-byte metatiles, choose the tile pair by quarter-cell coordinate and merge the matching attribute nibble into eight attribute bytes. Repeat to the configured sample limit.
; Split a 32-byte horizontal tile span at the nametable edge and derive the matching attribute spans.
; Compute the vertical tile count to the attribute boundary, its wrapped remainder and the attribute destination/phase. Clear the eight-byte attribute merge buffer.
; Jump through the sampler callback; the following entry selects map bank two for the leading sampler.
; Index three-byte map descriptors by scene coordinate. Low three bits choose the PRG selector; upper bits select the resource header, and the second descriptor byte selects the leading cell group.
; Scale the group by eight, add the header base, then select an eight-byte cell-index row. Save the metatile record base separately. The later entry selects map bank two for the trailing sampler.
; Resolve the same three-byte descriptor using its third byte for the trailing cell group.

; Select bank two before reading scene map metadata.

; Load the resource CHR selector and test whether palette selection is overridden.
; Select bank two for the palette override; the adjacent continuation resolves the palette selection.
; Send the saved byte through the shared PPU output helper.
; Load the selected resource palette pointer and copy sixteen colors.
; Sixteen byte lengths followed by sixteen little-endian handler words. Record tag selects both length and handler; values outside the finite table are not validated by the scanner.
; Record lengths, indexed by the unscaled tag.
; Handler words, indexed by twice the tag.
; Select bank two and service the interaction cooldown; a zero cooldown permits scanning the header interaction list.
; Count down the delay and reenter interaction completion when it expires.
; Skip scanning during transition; clear an interaction phase bit and load list pointer/count from the scene header.
; Use the interaction record opcode to index the sixteen-word handler table; the corresponding byte-length table controls record advancement.

; Advance the interaction pointer by the opcode's table length, decrement the record budget and continue scanning. Handler entries interpret position/orientation fields, configure linked actors, set scene flags, select resources, rescue targets or interaction cooldowns. A handler may return immediately when it consumes an action rather than continue the scan.
; Choose one of two vertical-bound fields according to which side of the encoded horizontal boundary contains the player.
; When snapped to the interaction position, choose its action byte according to horizontal direction.
; On overlap, initialize the selected linked actor or special slot and install its resource/palette state.
; Match position, direction and optional form bits before setting a player mode bit or switching form resources.
; Require the selected form and a fresh interaction latch before requesting the record text.
; Copy three consecutive record bytes into the shared interaction parameter cells.

; Require close overlap and matching direction, then set the common/player cooldown cells from the record.

; Interpret interaction tags after cooldown: tag thirteen consumes the remaining-attempt counter or enters a terminal script, restores saved scene coordinates and moves the player; other tags gate on companion flags or queue action bits.
; Toggle the horizontal direction bit and reset both player cooldowns to 16.
; For tag fourteen and prior tag ten, choose a saved position by scene/origin and request audio/action state.
; Use the common restore path with a 16-frame cooldown.
; Save interaction tag, auxiliary selector, player/scene coordinates and reversed direction for return. Tag ten checks stage/flag masks before starting an interaction.
; Load the chosen stage actor resource, queue text 47 and join the common restore continuation.

; Read the selected eight-byte palette group through the upper-bank pointer, then restore the saved PRG selector.
; Clear player overlay mode and initialize actor slot six from the interaction record.
; Select interaction overlay state one and join the common post-configuration path.
; Mark the special actor pair inactive, clear overlap selection and initialize player slot zero from the interaction record.
; Save player horizontal coordinates as camera state, take the interaction direction field, set player/scene flags and install the ordinary scene-update continuation.

; Twelve selector bytes followed by seven little-endian descriptor words, consumed by the interaction actor configurator. The following handler is a code barrier; masked possible indices do not establish an eighth pointer.
; Selector bytes.
; Seven descriptor words; the next byte starts a handler.

; Measure the player against a sign-dependent interaction strip. If close enough, save the target camera coordinate; on crossing, transform all six actors around the strip, rotating their directions by a quarter turn. Separate helpers test exact/snapped position, bounded horizontal/vertical overlap and copy three encoded coordinates to an actor with zero fractional cells.
; Compare the player horizontal coordinate, snapped to a four-pixel boundary, with the encoded interaction position.
; Return zero when an unblocked, grounded player lies within the supplied horizontal and vertical radius; return FF otherwise.
; Copy three encoded coordinate bytes into the actor, clearing both fractional coordinate cells.
; Set motion/input cooldowns, restore saved player and scene coordinates, clear fractions and a scene flag, resume configured speed/direction and reload the scene palette.

; Clear player interaction bits and restore companion/audio state once the current sound finishes, then reinstall normal scene updating. The second entry initializes an alternate text box, clears eight layout cells, selects palette/attributes and schedules drawing.
; Clear eight layout cells, install the alternate text palette/attributes and initialize its row buffer before screen drawing.

; Initialize the text renderer, then force layout variant two. The always-taken BNE skips the inline parameter bytes, whose lookup base overlaps its displacement; do not decode those bytes as fallthrough code.

; Eight layout parameter cells read through CPU $B6B5,Y. Index zero would be the preceding BNE displacement, retained as Code; LDX #2 makes the branch skip this suffix. The visible loop consumes Y=8 down to 1; index zero is the overlapping base byte and is not consumed by this loop. Parameter meanings are only partly recovered.
; Initialize text rendering and choose layout by scene parity. Copy twelve palette colors and eight trailing layout parameters, then initialize the nibble-addressed text stream.
; Read a packed layout byte and combine its fields with the existing index to choose the upper-bank layout resource.
; Read the layout resource pointer; header bit five chooses the destination half.
; Use a 22-byte destination offset for the alternate half.
; Expand signed repeat/literal packets into a ten-by-ten tile area with 32-byte row stride. Negative headers repeat a byte; nonnegative headers copy header+1 literals.
; Carry a repeated-byte output pointer into its high byte.
; Count ten columns, skip 22 bytes to the next row and stop after ten rows. Packet completion advances the source by two; literal setup follows at a separate entry.
; Carry the literal source pointer into its high byte.
; Copy one source byte to the tile buffer and advance both pointers.
; Carry the literal destination pointer into its high byte.
; Wrap at ten columns/rows; continue the packet or fetch another header. Restore normal resource bank when the layout finishes.
; Fill three eight-byte attribute staging rows using the layout-selected template.
; Use the alternate attribute template.
; Continue the digit extraction loop until the packed indicator has been consumed.
; Resolve the tile-buffer origin, choose width/row metadata from layout tables and yield through the text timing helper.
; Initialize the selected text stream, draw its box and choose marker glyphs according to layout orientation.
; Choose the wide-layout marker placement from the box width; the subtraction deliberately starts with carry clear.
; Write the two selected marker tiles, then restore resources.
; Resolve the box origin and, when page counters are nonzero, prepare the page indicator tile.
; Extract current/total packed page counters into the indicator glyph and repeat until both digits are consumed.
; Store the row terminator at offset 64 in the overlay buffer.
; Tail-call overlay setup. Later entries fill three attribute rows and initialize text state/buffer pointers from the selected text identifier.
; Preserve existing text state and jump to the current stream setup.
; Clear text page/selector state, copy default parameter pairs and optionally swap them according to scene parity.
; Exchange the paired selection parameters for the opposite parity, retaining both members before advancing to the next pair.
; Complete the paired parameter exchange and repeat for the remaining parameter index.
; Ensure a nonzero variant-selection mask before random selection.
; Enable all four variants when the mask was empty.
; Use two feedback-random bits to choose an allowed variant.
; Cycle the two-bit variant index until its mask bit is permitted.

; Store the chosen variant, derive scene/variant parameter pointers and load the text stream pointer. Clear ten 32-byte tile rows to spaces. A later entry computes a box-relative destination from layout header fields.
; Choose the alternate origin without the ten-column offset.
; Add the layout-specific origin to the tile buffer base and return its pointer.
; Draw a left tile, repeated center tile and right tile across the configured width; choose the row builder by width.
; Advance to the narrow box row helper, which centers the row by shifting bytes backward and padding spaces.
; Append the selected layout glyph, advance the text column and join either row wrap or further decoding.
; Advance rows, yield on even rows and stop at the configured last row. Place final border or body tiles; paging flags alter available text columns.
; Reserve columns according to page state and box width.
; Resolve pending/end-of-stream flags, fetch another text token group as needed and prepare blank padding when the row cannot hold it.
; Choose narrow-layout wrapping only below width fifteen.
; Center the narrow row using the bounded overlap-safe shift/pad helper.
; Mark row completion, fill spaces through the right edge and append its border tile before continuing rows.
; Test whether the decoded token length fits the remaining row width.
; Route an overflowing token to row wrapping.
; Clear row-complete state, copy the decoded token buffer and resume row processing.
; Append one space before the next token. A separate entry advances the destination by 32 and increments the row.

; Compute half the unused box width, rounded upward. Copy row bytes backward to make room, pad the left side with spaces and return the shifted column; backward copying preserves overlapping source/destination bytes.
; Initialize text state for direct line rendering and prepare the stream.
; Decode and copy token groups, pad each line with spaces, and continue at the configured width until stream completion. Restore the saved resource bank at exit.
; Clear output length; when a repeated token is active, decode it and decrement its repetition count. Nested stream state may resume after the repetition completes.
; Consume a nibble after the repeat when nested text state allows it.
; Operands below four enter the short control handler, update repeat state and append; larger operands take the packed-byte reader.
; Return with the decoded token buffer and length.
; Clear the deferred flag and resume command decoding.
; Pop a saved text stream when its nested flag is set.
; Read one nibble and partition it into control, repeat, nested-reference or extended-command classes.
; Route command nibbles twelve through fifteen to the extended handler.
; Combine command low bits with another nibble into a repeat count or reference index. Nested references also read a full pointer and may save the parent stream.
; Mark indexed-reference mode and initialize the referenced text stream.
; Read the next nibble with bank rollover handling and resume the page decoder.
; Read a two-byte nested stream pointer and test whether the indexed-reference setup already saved the parent.
; Clear indexed-reference mode and join the pointer switch.
; Save the caller text state, mark a nested stream and install its pointer.
; Install the decoded repeat count and return to token generation.
; Control commands two/three may set the interaction selector; clear the wait sign bit and mark text completion.
; Page-mode flag determines whether another control nibble is consumed; the continuation handles nested pointers and page origin state.
; Store page counters and copy the current nibble pointer as the next page's origin.
; Read the extended command operand as a packed byte before saving its page origin and nested pointer state.
; Read the second packed pointer byte while preserving the first on stack, then install the new nibble pointer.
; Compute the final text row when paged layout is active, then mark end-of-stream.
; Adjust the final row count for narrow text boxes.
; Save the final row and set the text-complete flag.

; Decode nibble tokens into the glyph buffer through lookup pages. Escape twelve extends a glyph into page $10; thirteen and fourteen select alternate glyph/control paths. Zero terminates a group. Output length is tracked independently of the stream pointer.
; Return from the zero escape operand.
; Choose glyph page $20; the substitution-mode flag can suppress a small control glyph.
; Append a glyph from the selected lookup page and increment output length.
; Return after the selected escape glyph.
; Append a page-$20 glyph for escape operands five and above, then rejoin ordinary glyph output.
; Select glyph page 32 and rejoin the ordinary output loop.
; Escape fourteen selects substitution handling; other tokens use the next control path.
; Read the substitution operand; zero selects a fixed glyph.
; Append lookup glyph $30 and continue the bounded lookup loop.
; Rejoin the common text output loop after escape handling.
; Codes below four select a small parameter group; larger codes select indexed nested text.
; Use four-byte parameter groups and the substitution-mode flag; selectors one through three append nonzero group bytes until their terminator.
; Advance the lookup index and repeat while it remains nonzero.
; If output already exists, rewind the control token; otherwise use operand-minus-four as a nested reference index.
; Rewind when a token must be deferred until the next group; otherwise consume its operand.
; Read the next control nibble and dispatch extended escapes to dictionary or nested/RAM pointer handling.

; Extended escape fifteen selects a nested stream. Special selectors clear a variant bit, advance the variant, or cycle through active rescue masks; ordinary selectors use RAM pointer pairs. Install the nested pointer and its text-state flag before restoring text bank context. Other escape operands map to dictionary entries 12..26.
; Use the next active rescue mask bit to select its nested text pointer and update page counters.
; Read a little-endian nested nibble pointer from the RAM parameter-pair array.
; Set the nested-stream flag and restore text bank context before decoding resumes.
; Enter the indexed text reference selected by the substitution code.
; Temporarily enable substitution mode, decode a glyph group, clear the mode and restore the parent stream.
; Read the next escape and append a small page-$20 glyph when permitted; defer other controls by rewinding.
; Consume the substitution escape operand and copy the selected zero-terminated parameter group into the token buffer.
; For substitution selectors 1..3, copy the chosen four-byte group's nonzero bytes into the token buffer until the zero terminator; retain the resulting token length.
; Rewind one extra nibble before the shared deferred-control return.
; Rewind a deferred token. A separate entry appends ordinary page-selected glyphs; page-$20 low codes terminate the group early.
; Terminate the glyph group for page-$20 codes below five.
; Continue reading glyph nibbles for this group.
; Save flags, repeat count and nibble pointer into parallel eight-slot arrays indexed by nesting depth. Callers must keep nesting bounded; no overflow guard is visible here.
; Restore the previous text stream and depth. The separate initialization entry chooses PRG selector six/seven from pointer sign, maps nibble address to CPU $C000–$FFFF and primes the cached byte.
; Preserve reference index and push caller state; select bank six when required before the pointer-table lookup.

; Read a little-endian stream pointer at $C000+2*index and initialize it. A separate entry increments the nibble pointer and returns the old nibble, switching resource selectors at the explicit boundary.
; At nibble pointer $7FC0 switch to $8000 and PRG selector seven; this special packed-domain boundary is not a generic CPU address wrap.
; Odd nibble addresses use cached low nibble; even addresses fetch a byte and return its high nibble. The separate rewind entry decrements the packed pointer.
; On backward crossing at $7FFF, replace low byte with $BF and select PRG six to mirror the special forward boundary.
; Reload cached byte only when the original nibble parity requires it.
; Return with the rewound text state.
; Prime the cached packed byte through the address conversion helper.

; Read two nibbles as one byte at either parity. Aligned reads return the cache; unaligned reads combine its low nibble with the next byte high nibble. The separate pointer advance entry adds two packed positions.
; Check whether the two-nibble advance crossed the special $7FC0 bank boundary.
; Return without a bank change.
; Keep pointer parity, move into the $8000 packed domain and select PRG seven.
; Preserve A/Y/X and replace both NMI continuations temporarily. Wait for the sprite-zero split, switch graphics and release the busy flag so text generation can yield to another NMI before resuming.

; Restore scene CHR selectors in the temporary first continuation. The second continuation discards its interrupt return stack entries and restores the text resource bank before returning to the suspended decoder; this depends on the exact NMI stack contract.
; Choose PRG six for a nonnegative packed pointer.
; Choose PRG seven for a negative packed pointer.
; Restore the decoder register stack and return to its caller.

; Three four-byte zero-terminated substitution groups, a 49-byte glyph lookup, and four default parameter bytes copied as two pairs. Packed text consumers establish these roles; the final parameter bytes are not instructions.
; Parameter groups; each group occupies four bytes including terminator/padding.
; Glyph lookup.
; Default parameter pairs.

; Uniform byte run bounded by changed neighboring bytes; prior byte/pattern and boundary review supports generic Data. Exact fill purpose or consumer is unresolved. Neighboring regions retain their own classifications.
; Reset MMC1 shift state through an RMW at $FFFF; then serially select control $1A before jumping through the fixed lower-bank reset pointer.
; Load MMC1 control value $1A, establishing fixed lower PRG pair and switchable upper pair.
; Write one control bit to MMC1.
; Shift the next control bit into position.
; Continue the serial control writes until the shifted value reaches zero.
; Jump through the fixed lower-bank reset pointer at $BFF6.
; Jump through the fixed lower-bank NMI pointer at $BFF4.
; Jump through the fixed lower-bank IRQ pointer at $BFF8.

In the fixed lower bank the software pointers resolve NMI/reset/IRQ; other copies contain the bank tag/zero words. Hardware vectors select the replicated $FFEE/$FFE0/$FFF1 trampolines. CPU aliases depend on MMC1 context.
; Three seven-word little-endian resource pointer arrays followed by seven CHR selectors. Screen resource loader indexes all columns with the same screen selector.

; Install a rendering-disabled continuation, clear palette/nametables, then read PPU addresses and literal byte runs from descriptor-selected resources. Negative bytes delimit runs; $FF ends the screen resource. Restore its palette/CHR and enter scene display setup.

; Seven literal screen streams: coordinate pair, nonnegative glyph bytes, 80 row marker and FF end marker. The auxiliary bytes after the last terminator have no established consumer or schema; stage/coordinate/sound columns then precede the scene object updater.
; Auxiliary bytes C220..C22B: repeated tile-like values and ordered nibbles; neighboring consumers/roots give no exact consumer or schema.

; Update paired scene display records, pulse sweep state and bounded decorative-object slots. Packed timers choose frame/subframe; signed fractional velocity advances coordinates. Stage thresholds and viewport bounds retire objects; random selectors below nine choose descriptor/flag columns and initial motion. Rendering preserves X across the shared sprite helper. Original visual identities remain uncertain.

; Scene renderer descriptor/flag columns, twelve command strides and a twelve-word command dispatch table precede seven scripts. Scripts have six-byte headers and commands sized by the stride table; the final command 9 ends at the next independently known resource.

; Six-byte header, then stride-sized commands through command 9.
; Six-byte header, then stride-sized commands through command 9.
; Six-byte header, then stride-sized commands through command 9.
; Six-byte header, then stride-sized commands through command 9.
; Six-byte header, then stride-sized commands through command 9.
; Six-byte header, then stride-sized commands through command 9.

; Two 23-byte descriptors contain three pointer pairs, braking/speed bias/acceleration, animation counts and frames, airborne timing/terrain limits, three actor-shape values and a landing callback. Five six-cell stage selector rows follow, then eleven eight-cell parallel form fields and contact candidate/extent columns.
; Start the three-entry resource contact list. Skip disabled/elevated candidates before computing pairwise displacement.
; Subtract candidate coordinates from actor X into signed horizontal and vertical differences; the zero candidate uses the alternate comparison path.
; Use the contacted actor animation frame plus one to index the adjacent extent test.
; Compare signed horizontal displacement against the candidate-specific contact threshold.
; Compare signed contact coordinate differences against the positive/negative extent columns; branch to contact handling only within the accepted bounds.
; Advance through the bounded candidate list, then clear actor contact bit 5 and return.

; Reject already handled contacts, set the contact flag and distinguish player from actor contacts. Player modes select one of three bounded callback words; mask 06 alone does not prove a valid fourth entry.
; Exactly three little-endian callback words. The consumer masks with 06, but selector 6 would overread into code and is not asserted valid.

; Contact callbacks restore ordinary actor state, start player animation, consume a packed counter or choose stage-dependent rewards. The reward selector table supplies only offsets 0/2/4 to the three handler words. Natural gameplay selection is not established.
; Three little-endian callbacks selected by offsets 0,2,4 from the independently bounded stage/random table.
; Bound the random selector to four entries and request the selected sound.
; Four sound tags selected by the low two bits of the reward value.
; Use stage-row item/dialogue tables to select the item text or scene text pointer; preserve the bounded item index for the shared output helpers.
; Four variant offsets followed by six stage base offsets, combined to index dialogue pointer rows.
; Use the contacted actor frame selector to dispatch through four callback words.
; Four little-endian contact callback words; repeated return-only destinations are intentional.
; Clear the partner slot, update interaction flags and unlink paired actors, or install the timed actor animation while marking the special contact state.
; Six eight-cell rows of handler offsets (only 0/2/4), six sixteen-cell item rows, six sixteen-cell dialogue rows and six palette pointer words. Each consumer uses its own bounded row width.

; Multiple entries upload horizontal tile strips, vertical strips with PPU increment 32, and masked attribute strips. Horizontal attributes preserve the opposite nibble using buffered PPU reads; vertical attributes use eight-byte address strides. Transfer lengths come from the split descriptors built in the fixed bank.

; Initialize inventory maxima and stage masks, clear three saved target slots and twelve distribution slots, then choose distinct targets/locations. Parity restricts the candidate group; occupied masks and target tags reject unsuitable candidates. Each selected target receives one of four random subslots; fill remaining slots with unique nibble selectors. Loops rely on stage tables providing enough valid candidates.
; Fill every unused distribution cell with a unique random nibble selector; increment modulo sixteen to avoid duplicates.

; Cap the fallback resource selector at sixteen.
; Load paired resource pointers for the clamped fallback selector.

; Unpack two two-bit selectors from saved scene state, select paired resource pointers, then load two six-byte parameter rows using scene*24 and selector*6. Finish the eight-pointer table with fixed fallbacks.
; Expand four packed bytes into eight high/low nibbles in scratch; phone matching uses the first seven digits.

; Mixed stage masks, packed phone digits, text pointers and four-byte action/NMI records. Phone matching and text dispatch establish their data role; individual record extents are retained only where a finite consumer supplies them.
; Select the phone continuation by UI mode, hide the first OAM entry and restore the palette. Resume normal NMI return or the alternate scene path according to the mode flag.
; Three little-endian NMI continuation words selected by the even phone UI mode; each returns through the interrupt epilogue.
; Set phone mode four, initialize selection, draw the inventory counts/icons and cursor, then return through the interrupt epilogue.
; Choose keypad mode, initialize the phone UI, clear entered-digit count and render its cursor.
; Reset phone selection, load the screen resources and digit display, initialize phone state, copy OAM by DMA and return to the foreground loop.

; Queue a UI sound, clear scroll/nametable state, load the mode-selected screen and palette and install UI continuations. A separate display entry transfers OAM/palette and dispatches mode-specific PPU work.
; Three little-endian transfer callbacks indexed by phone mode 0,2,4.

; Scan eight controller masks, latch newly pressed keys and dispatch through a button-by-mode table with six-byte rows. Released keys clear their latches. After all keys, dispatch the mode frame callback.
; Eight controller masks, twenty-four callback words indexed as six bytes per button plus mode 0/2/4, then three per-mode frame callbacks.
; Save the mode index, install its continuation pair and disable rendering while the next screen is prepared.

; Five PPU count destinations, twelve PPU icon destinations, sixty-four glyph cells, sixteen item glyphs, four count cells and sixteen sprite-address bytes. Inventory and icon drawing consume these separate columns.

; Draw five packed decimal inventory counts at PPU destinations, suppressing leading zeroes. Scan sixteen rescue mask bits to draw up to twelve icons, then draw the additional counted icons. The following cursor routine draws the selected phone column and optional button marker before sprite finalization.
; Four cursor X positions, one per inventory column.
; Choose mode two and enter the shared mode installer.
; Increment or decrement the phone selection within its bounds when no selection animation is active; set direction/state flags, start the eight-tick delay and redraw.
; When no decoder chunk is pending, blink the selected palette or route to a multi-step palette animation.
; Every eight ticks advance or retreat the signed animation selector; normalize its terminal value to zero and update the displayed record.
; Run the buffered decoder, update displayed phonebook text and render the selection sprite.
; Four four-byte records: little-endian stream start and end. The phone selection chooses one record for the PPU decoder.
; Use a four-byte start/end record for the selected phone animation, initialize the PPU chunk width, alternate the nametable base and tail-call the stream decoder.
; Sixteen phone UI glyph/attribute values, between the bounded stream helper and the next known code entry.
; Upload pending decoder output when its chunk count is nonzero.
